test_plan.scope: Validate FR-030..FR-038 (subnet detection, ICMP sweep, ARP pairing, OUI lookup, persistence, online/offline state machine, JSON API, /network UI fragment, self-throttle) plus NFR-011..NFR-015 (privilege boundary, embedded OUI, SQLite reuse, performance budget, UX tokens).
test_plan.approach: Three-layer pyramid. Unit tests pin pure logic (subnet parser, ARP parser, OUI lookup, state machine). Integration tests exercise the orchestrator + store + SQLite together with a faked ICMP transport. Two e2e tests run the real HTTP handlers against an in-process server with a pre-populated DB.
fixtures: fakeICMPTransport — deterministic per-host reply map; supports drop-after-N-cycles for offline tests
tmpDB — t.TempDir() SQLite per test, no shared state
/proc/net/arp synthetic file — written into a t.TempDir() and read via an injected path resolver
/proc/net/route synthetic file — same injection seam as arp
exclusions: No tests for per-device WiFi signal, bandwidth, mDNS, IPv6, fingerprinting, SNMP, or alerting — all in no_go_zone.
No live-network tests that depend on actual LAN devices; all integration TCs use injected /proc files and a fake ICMP transport.
No tests against the real IEEE OUI registry over the network; OUI table is the bundled artifact.
No tests for database backup mechanics — covered by parent FR-015 tests.

test_cases.title: Subnet detector returns 192.168.1.0/24 from a synthetic /proc/net/route + eth0 inet
preconditions: subnet.Detect() accepts injectable readers for /proc/net/route and net.InterfaceByName
test_cases.given: /proc/net/route contains a default-route line for eth0 (destination 0.0.0.0, gateway 0101A8C0) and net.InterfaceByName('eth0').Addrs() returns 192.168.1.42/24
test_cases.then: returns Subnet{CIDR:'192.168.1.0/24', Iface:'eth0', Status:'ok'} with no error
steps: Inject a fake interface resolver returning 192.168.1.42/24 for eth0
test_cases.expected_result: Subnet.CIDR == '192.168.1.0/24'; Iface == 'eth0'; Status == 'ok'; err == nil

test_cases.title: Subnet detector reports no-default-route when /proc/net/route has no default entry
test_cases.given: /proc/net/route contains only header + a non-default route (destination 192.168.1.0, gateway 0)
test_cases.then: returns Subnet{Status:'no-default-route'} with no error and CIDR empty
steps: Write synthetic /proc/net/route lacking a default entry
test_cases.expected_result: Status == 'no-default-route'; CIDR == ''; err == nil

test_cases.title: Subnet detector clamps a /16 interface to the host's /24
test_cases.given: Interface eth0 has 10.50.7.42/16 and a default route via that interface
test_cases.then: returns Subnet{CIDR:'10.50.7.0/24', Status:'subnet-clamped'}
steps: Assert clamped CIDR and status flag
test_cases.expected_result: CIDR == '10.50.7.0/24'; Status == 'subnet-clamped'

test_cases.title: Sweep emits exactly 254 ICMP probes against a /24 and completes within 3 s wall-clock
preconditions: fakeICMPTransport answers 30 hosts with 5 ms RTT, others with timeout
test_cases.given: Orchestrator started with subnet 192.168.1.0/24, cadence 60 s, fakeICMPTransport, 32-worker pool
test_cases.then: transport.SendCount() == 254 (one per host address 1..254); orchestrator.LastSweepDuration() < 3 s
test_cases.expected_result: SendCount == 254; LastSweepDuration < 3 * time.Second

test_cases.title: Overlapping sweep cycle is skipped and overrun counter increments
test_cases.given: Orchestrator with cadence 1 s and a transport that blocks the in-flight sweep for 2 s
test_cases.when: the cadence ticker fires while the prior sweep is still running
test_cases.then: no new sweep starts; orchestrator.OverrunCount() == 1; only one cycle's SendCount is observed
steps: Configure 1 s cadence and a transport with a 2 s artificial delay
Inspect overrun counter and total SendCount
test_cases.expected_result: OverrunCount == 1; total SendCount == 254 (single cycle, not 2 cycles)

test_cases.title: Sweep cadence configured to 1800 s is honoured within ±10% over 3 cycles
test_cases.given: Orchestrator with cadence 1800 s and fake clock advancing 5400 s in 3 cycle steps
test_cases.then: interval between sweep starts is 1800 s ±180 s (±10%) for both gaps
test_cases.expected_result: All 2 inter-sweep intervals within [1620 s, 1980 s]

test_cases.title: ARP parser pairs 5 responding IPs with their MACs from /proc/net/arp
test_cases.given: Synthetic /proc/net/arp with 5 entries, all flag 0x2 (REACHABLE), MACs distinct; sweep responders set is the same 5 IPs
test_cases.then: returns 5 (ip, mac) pairs matching the file; mac strings normalised to lower-hex with colons
test_cases.expected_result: len(pairs) == 5; each mac matches expected lower-hex form

test_cases.title: Missing /proc/net/arp degrades gracefully (mac=null), no panic
test_cases.given: arpPath points to a file that does not exist; 3 responding IPs
test_cases.then: returns 3 pairs with mac == '' and a sentinel error errors.Is(err, ErrARPUnavailable); orchestrator log line emitted exactly once
steps: Assert mac == '' on each, sentinel error, and log captured once
test_cases.expected_result: All pair.MAC == ''; errors.Is(err, ErrARPUnavailable) == true; log line count == 1

test_cases.title: Stale ARP entries (flag 0x0) are ignored
test_cases.given: /proc/net/arp with 3 reachable (0x2) and 2 incomplete (0x0) entries; all 5 IPs are responders
test_cases.then: returns 5 pairs; the 2 with flag 0x0 have mac == '' and status 'no-arp', the 3 with flag 0x2 have full MACs
test_cases.expected_result: 3 entries with mac populated; 2 entries with mac == '' and status 'no-arp'

test_cases.title: OUI lookup resolves B8:27:EB to a vendor string containing 'Raspberry Pi'
test_cases.given: Bundled OUI table loaded at startup (go:embed)
test_cases.then: returns a string containing 'Raspberry Pi' (case-insensitive)
steps: Call oui.Vendor on canonical Pi MAC
test_cases.expected_result: strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(vendor), 'raspberry pi') == true

test_cases.title: Locally-administered MAC (LAA bit set) returns 'Locally administered' regardless of OUI
test_cases.given: MAC 02:00:00:00:00:01 (LAA bit set in first byte: 0x02 has bit 1 set)
test_cases.then: returns 'Locally administered'
test_cases.expected_result: vendor == 'Locally administered'

test_cases.title: Unknown OUI returns 'Unknown' (no error)
test_cases.given: MAC 00:DE:AD:BE:EF:01 with OUI 00:DE:AD not in the bundled table
test_cases.then: returns 'Unknown' without error
test_cases.expected_result: vendor == 'Unknown'

test_cases.title: Persistence — first sweep inserts new MAC with first_seen == last_seen and online=true
preconditions: Empty t.TempDir() SQLite DB initialised with parent schema + lan_devices table
test_cases.given: lan_devices table is empty; sweep observes (mac=AA:BB:CC:11:22:33, ip=192.168.1.50, vendor='Acme Corp')
test_cases.when: store.Upsert is called for the observation
test_cases.then: row exists with first_seen == last_seen (within 1 ms), online == 1, missed_sweeps == 0
test_cases.expected_result: Single row; |first_seen - last_seen| < 1 ms; online == 1; missed_sweeps == 0

test_cases.title: DHCP renewal — same MAC with new IP updates ip and last_seen, preserves first_seen
preconditions: DB pre-populated with one row: mac=AA:BB:CC:11:22:33, ip=192.168.1.50, first_seen=t0, last_seen=t0
test_cases.given: 1 hour later, sweep observes the same MAC with ip=192.168.1.99
test_cases.then: row's ip becomes '192.168.1.99'; last_seen advances; first_seen still equals t0
steps: Pre-populate DB with original row at t0
Advance fake clock by 1 hour to t1
test_cases.expected_result: ip == '192.168.1.99'; last_seen ≈ t1; first_seen == t0 (unchanged)

test_cases.title: Persistence survives process restart — first_seen preserved across re-open
test_cases.given: DB has one row inserted 3 days ago (first_seen = t-3d)
test_cases.when: the *DB is closed and re-opened, then SELECT runs against the new handle
test_cases.then: first_seen still equals t-3d (no clock-on-startup overwrite)
steps: Open DB, insert row with first_seen=t-3d
test_cases.expected_result: first_seen == original t-3d value

test_cases.title: Single-miss tolerance — device missing 1 sweep then responding stays online
preconditions: Default miss threshold N=3
test_cases.given: Device AA:BB online from sweeps 1-2; sweep 3 misses; sweep 4 sees it again
test_cases.then: after sweep 4 the row's online == 1, missed_sweeps == 0, last_seen advanced to sweep 4 timestamp
steps: Drive 4 sweep cycles via the orchestrator with the fake transport
Sweep 3: device is in the drop list
After sweep 4: SELECT row and assert
test_cases.expected_result: online == 1; missed_sweeps == 0; last_seen == sweep 4 ts

test_cases.title: Three consecutive misses flip device to offline; last_seen freezes
test_cases.given: Device online at sweep 1; absent from sweeps 2, 3, 4 (N=3)
test_cases.then: row's online == 0; last_seen == sweep 1 timestamp (frozen, not sweep 4); missed_sweeps == 3
steps: Run 4 sweeps; device is in the responder set only on sweep 1
Assert online flip and last_seen freeze
test_cases.expected_result: online == 0; last_seen == sweep 1 ts; missed_sweeps == 3

test_cases.title: Recovery — offline device responding once flips back to online
test_cases.given: Device flipped offline at sweep 4 (per previous TC); sweep 5 sees it again
test_cases.then: row's online == 1; missed_sweeps == 0; last_seen advances to sweep 5 ts; first_seen unchanged
steps: Bring DB into the offline state at sweep 4
Run sweep 5 with the device in the responder set
test_cases.expected_result: online flips back to 1; missed_sweeps == 0; last_seen == sweep 5 ts; first_seen unchanged

test_cases.title: GET /api/network/lan-devices returns JSON with online entries first
preconditions: DB pre-populated: 2 online (last_seen recent), 1 offline (last_seen 1h ago)
test_cases.given: An authenticated session and 3 rows in lan_devices
test_cases.when: GET /api/network/lan-devices is issued with the session cookie and Accept: application/json
test_cases.then: HTTP 200; JSON array length 3; first 2 entries have online=true; third has online=false; ordering within online is last_seen DESC; timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC
steps: Assert status, length, ordering, ISO 8601 format
test_cases.expected_result: Status 200; len(JSON) == 3; arr[0].online && arr[1].online && !arr[2].online; arr[0].last_seen > arr[1].last_seen

test_cases.title: Unauthenticated GET returns 401 (JSON) / redirect (HTML)
test_cases.given: No session cookie
test_cases.then: HTTP 401 with body containing 'unauthenticated' (or parent's standard JSON error shape)
test_cases.expected_result: Status == 401; body matches parent auth-error contract

test_cases.title: API returns within 100 ms p99 over 100 sequential requests on a 30-device DB
preconditions: DB pre-populated with 30 rows
test_cases.given: An authenticated session and 30 rows in lan_devices
test_cases.then: p99 latency < 100 ms (computed from the slowest 1 of 100 = the 99th-percentile sample)

test_cases.title: /network page renders LAN devices table within 5 s with WAN events still present below it

test_cases.when: the operator opens /network in a headless browser
test_cases.then: within 5 s of page load, the lan-devices section shows a 5-row table; the WAN events block is also rendered below it; both regions are visible without scrolling on a 1280×800 viewport

Wait for the lan-devices section to populate
Assert the WAN-events block is also present and below the lan-devices section
test_cases.expected_result: Page load < 5 s; LAN table has 5 rows; WAN events block follows it

test_cases.title: Empty state — when no devices observed yet, /network shows the 'No devices discovered' message instead of an empty table

test_cases.title: Online badge contrast meets WCAG AA in both light and dark themes

test_cases.when: an axe-core scan runs against the page in both prefers-color-scheme: light and dark
test_cases.then: 0 contrast violations are reported on the lan-devices section in both themes
steps: Render /network with light theme media query
Assert 0 contrast violations in section both times
test_cases.expected_result: axe.violations(contrast) on lan-devices section == 0 in both themes

test_cases.title: Two consecutive over-budget sweeps trigger 2× cadence and self_throttled flag
test_cases.given: Orchestrator at cadence 300 s; transport configured to make sweeps take 4 s wall-clock for 2 cycles in a row
test_cases.then: next cadence is 600 s (2×); status.self_throttled == true; status flag visible via /api/network/lan-devices/status
steps: Configure orchestrator with slow transport for 2 cycles
test_cases.expected_result: next interval == 600 s; status.self_throttled == true

test_cases.title: 30 min of in-budget sweeps after throttling restores the configured cadence
preconditions: Orchestrator already in self-throttled state at cadence 600 s
test_cases.given: Throttled to 600 s; transport now completes sweeps in 1 s; fake clock runs 30 min of sweeps
test_cases.when: the 30 min of all-clear samples elapses
test_cases.then: next cadence returns to the configured 300 s baseline; status.self_throttled == false
steps: Set state to self-throttled at 600 s
test_cases.expected_result: Next interval == 300 s; status.self_throttled == false

test_cases.title: Cadence cap — repeated over-budget cycles never push interval above 1800 s
preconditions: Orchestrator at cadence 1200 s
test_cases.given: Throttling triggers twice in a row: first throttle would set 2400 s, second would set 4800 s
test_cases.when: the scheduler computes the next cadence after each over-budget cycle
test_cases.then: first throttle clamps to 1800 s; second throttle stays at 1800 s; status.self_throttled == true; no overflow into negative numbers or wraparound
steps: Assert clamp at 1800 s both times
test_cases.expected_result: After 1st throttle: interval == 1800 s; after 2nd throttle: interval == 1800 s (no overflow)

test_cases.title: [NFR-011] Deployed binary has no CAP_NET_RAW or other new capabilities (deployment proof)
preconditions: linux/arm64 binary built via 'make build-arm'
test_cases.given: the built binary at bin/ultron-ap-linux-arm64

test_cases.title: [NFR-011] Sweep fails closed when net.ipv4.ping_group_range is unset
preconditions: Linux test host where ping_group_range can be temporarily set to '1 0'
test_cases.given: ping_group_range is configured to disallow the running uid
test_cases.then: the sweep returns ErrUnprivilegedICMPUnavailable; no raw socket fallback is attempted; no panic; orchestrator logs once and self-disables

test_cases.expected_result: errors.Is(err, ErrUnprivilegedICMPUnavailable) == true; no raw-socket attempt; orchestrator.Disabled() == true

test_cases.title: [NFR-011] Unprivileged uid can read /proc/net/arp on the deployed Pi (privilege boundary holds)
preconditions: Test runs as a non-root uid
test_cases.given: Process is running as the unprivileged 'ultron' uid (or any non-root in tests)
test_cases.then: returns the parsed entries with no permission error; no setuid escalation, no helper IPC calls
steps: Drop to a non-root uid via os.Setuid in a fork (or assert os.Geteuid() != 0)
Assert no IPC call to ultron-helper was attempted (count == 0)

test_cases.title: [NFR-012] OUI lookup works in a process with no DNS / no outbound network

test_cases.when: oui.Vendor is called for B8:27:EB:00:00:00, 00:1A:11:00:00:00 (Google Inc), and a random unknown prefix

test_cases.title: [NFR-012] Malformed MAC input does not cause network lookup or panic
test_cases.given: MAC strings: 'not-a-mac', '00:00', 'ZZ:YY:XX:11:22:33', empty string
test_cases.then: each returns 'Unknown' or 'Locally administered' (depending on parse) without error and without any net syscall
steps: Install a net-syscall hook that fails the test on any DNS / connect call

test_cases.expected_result: All calls return a non-empty string; no panic; net syscall count == 0

test_cases.expected_result: Two runs produce byte-identical output; output matches the embedded path
